milestone.title: raul configurable keybinds via ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml — TUI-wide keymap with sane defaults

intent.outcome: raul loads a validated global and per-lane keyboard map from ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml, preserves hardcoded defaults when absent or invalid, supports atomic reload, and exposes the effective map read-only in Settings.

problem.description: Keybinds are hardcoded across global and lane dispatchers. Users need an override file without duplicating defaults or risking lockout. The plan therefore needs one action registry, one key parser, deterministic conflict handling, atomic reload, and a read-only Settings view; editing remains external.

in_scope: Typed action registry covering global actions and every lane action; TOML contains only overrides.
Canonical key/chord syntax shared with the existing parser, including documented aliases and modifiers.
Validation for unknown actions, malformed keys, duplicate bindings, reserved recovery keys, and per-section fallback.
Atomic startup/reload with previous-map retention on failure; SIGHUP on Unix plus an explicit in-app reload action on all supported platforms.
out_of_scope: In-app keymap editor, mouse bindings, and per-autopilot-role keymaps.
Macros, multi-key sequences, and conditional/contextual bindings beyond global plus active-lane sections.

acceptance_criteria.description: At startup one shared Keybinds service loads global and per-lane overrides. With no file, every existing default remains unchanged; lanes do not parse the file independently.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_action_registry --no-fail-fast exit 0 (10/10 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: A fixture remaps autopilot.pause to F1, reloads, and proves F1 invokes the canonical pause action while the prior Space binding no longer does; other actions retain defaults.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_override_dispatch --no-fail-fast exit 0 (5/5 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Unknown actions warn and are ignored; malformed keys or conflicting bindings reject only the affected section and retain its previous/default map. Diagnostics name section, action, and value without aborting raul.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_invalid_entries --no-fail-fast exit 0 (8/8 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Reload parses and validates a complete candidate before atomically swapping it. SIGHUP requests reload on Unix without doing I/O in the signal handler; an explicit reload action works on all platforms. Reload does not wait for user input, and failure preserves the previous map.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_reload --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Settings renders the effective global and per-lane map, marks overridden versus default bindings, and states the external TOML path; it provides no in-app editing affordance.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test settings_keybind_view --no-fail-fast exit 0 (7/7 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: The action registry enumerates every configurable global and lane action. Unknown names cannot shadow actions; global recovery actions remain reachable; duplicate key assignments within an active section are rejected with deterministic diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_action_registry --no-fail-fast exit 0 (10/10 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Parser regressions cover the full documented key surface: underscore and dash aliases, double_quote/double-quote, page_up/page-down, BackTab/Backtab/back-tab, mixed case, modifiers, and combinations such as Ctrl+double-quote and Ctrl+page-up.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybind_parser_aliases --no-fail-fast exit 0 (8/8 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Migration from existing project `keybinds.*` configuration is deterministic: user-level keybinds.toml overrides legacy project bindings, legacy bindings override hardcoded defaults, reads never rewrite either source, and use of the legacy source emits one migration hint.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test keybinds_v2 --no-fail-fast exit 0 (21/21 pass)

design_decisions.choice: TOML section per lane, action-name → key-code strings, default values live in code (not in a default-file).
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids the 'defaults drift from code' problem; the source-of-truth for defaults is the code, and the TOML is opt-in overrides.

design_decisions.choice: SIGHUP triggers reload (not inotify) because SIGHUP works on every platform (macOS, Linux, BSD) and is one signal; inotify would need a platform-specific watcher.
design_decisions.rationale: Cross-platform portability with one signal; the user can `killall -HUP raul` (or use the harness's hook) to reload.

design_decisions.choice: Unknown actions ignored + warn; unparseable key strings fall back to defaults. No abort on bad TOML.
design_decisions.rationale: A user typo shouldn't lock the user out of the app; defaults survive errors.

work_packages.name: Configurable keymap (TUI-wide)
work_packages.goal: TOML keymap config loads at startup; each lane reads its section; SIGHUP triggers live reload; Settings shows the active map.
work_packages.rollback: Revert keybinds.toml loading to a no-op; full regression stays green.

work_packages.name: Registry and parser
work_packages.goal: Define complete configurable actions, canonical key syntax, and deterministic validation/conflict behavior.
work_packages.rollback: Keep hardcoded dispatch and ignore the optional override file.

work_packages.name: Integration, reload, and visibility
work_packages.goal: Apply one validated map across dispatchers, reload atomically, and display effective bindings.
work_packages.rollback: Disable reload and override application while retaining defaults.

findings.description: Production startup does not load the user-level keybinds.toml. runner.rs:409 calls Keybinds::load(runner), which reads only the legacy [keybinds] JSON via load_from_config. The M222 layered loader Keybinds::load_effective (keybinds.rs:1890) is library-only — no production caller. TOML applies only on SIGHUP (runner.rs:451) or Action::ReloadKeybinds (action.rs:926). Violates AC-01 ('At startup one shared Keybinds service loads global and per-lane overrides'), AC-08 ('user-level keybinds.toml overrides legacy project bindings'), and docs/raul/keybinds.md ('raul reads ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml ... at startup').
findings.author: reviewer-222
findings.summary: User-level ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml is not loaded at startup
findings.rationale: AC-01 says 'At startup one shared Keybinds service loads global and per-lane overrides'; docs/raul/keybinds.md (lines 138-141) says 'raul reads ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml ... at startup'; AC-08 says 'user-level keybinds.toml overrides legacy project bindings'. But the production startup path is runner.rs:409 -> Keybinds::load(runner), which only reads the legacy [keybinds] JSON section via load_from_config. The user-level TOML is loaded only inside the on_idle hook at runner.rs:450 when SIGHUP flips the flag, or via Action::ReloadKeybinds at action.rs:926. The M222 layered loader Keybinds::load_effective (keybinds.rs:1890) composes the three layers and IS unit-tested in tests/keybinds_v2.rs, but is never called from any production code path. Concretely: a fresh  then  works (SIGHUP loads TOML), but a cold start with ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml present does NOT apply the override until the user SIGHUPs or triggers the explicit reload action. M225/M226 lesson applies: the override is unit-tested in isolation (10/10 keybind_action_registry, 21/21 keybinds_v2) but not wired into production startup. Fix: change Keybinds::load to read the TOML from Self::default_path() after the JSON step (or wrap with load_effective), then assign the layered result to app.keybinds at runner.rs:409. Add an integration test that writes ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml, calls Keybinds::load (or runs the startup sequence), and asserts the override applies.

findings.description: Settings lane does not render the new KeybindsView. Keybinds::view() and KeybindsView are defined (keybinds.rs:1356, 2248) but never called from any renderer. render_settings_lane (render/overlays.rs:358) renders only the legacy [keybinds] JSON config surface. AC-05 ('Settings renders the effective global and per-lane map, marks overridden versus default bindings, and states the external TOML path; it provides no in-app editing affordance') is library-tested only.
findings.author: reviewer-222
findings.summary: Settings view does not render the effective keymap / TOML path
findings.rationale: AC-05 says 'Settings renders the effective global and per-lane map, marks overridden versus default bindings, and states the external TOML path; it provides no in-app editing affordance.' But Keybinds::view() and KeybindsView (keybinds.rs:1356, 2248) are library-only — no renderer calls them. The production Settings lane is render_settings_lane (render/overlays.rs:358), which renders the legacy [keybinds] JSON config surface via state.schema + flat_key (modes/settings.rs:16) + keybind_default_label (modes/settings.rs:208). No row shows 'effective vs default', no override marker, no TOML path string. The Autopilot lane's [autopilot] actions are not in SETTINGS_KEYS at all. The 7/7 settings_keybind_view tests pass at the library level (Keybinds::view() returns correct rows) but the renderer never invokes view(). M225/M226 lesson applies. Fix: thread app.keybinds.view() into render_settings_lane (or a sibling renderer) so the operator sees the effective map with override markers and the TOML path; remove the [keybinds] JSON rows from SETTINGS_KEYS (or keep both — but the TOML view must be reachable). Add an integration test that renders the Settings lane after a keybinds.toml override and asserts the F1 row is marked overridden and the TOML path is visible.

findings.description: F-01 regression tests exercise Keybinds::load_effective directly, not the new Keybinds::load_layered that runner.rs:417 wires. They pass for incidental reasons: a revert of runner.rs:417 from load_layered back to load would leave all 3 F-01 tests green. The test header comment ('exercises load_layered directly') is misleading. F-02 is properly production-path tested; F-01 is not.
findings.author: reviewer-222
findings.summary: F-01 regression tests pass for incidental reasons (test load_effective, not load_layered)
findings.rationale: Cycle 2 F-01 fix added Keybinds::load_layered (keybinds.rs:521) and wired it at runner.rs:417. The wiring is real and unconditional. But m222_f01_startup_loader.rs (3 tests) does not actually exercise load_layered -- every test calls Keybinds::load_effective(None, Some(&toml_text)) or Keybinds::load_effective(Some(&legacy_json), Some(&toml_text)) directly. The test header comment claims 'This suite exercises load_layered directly with a custom in-process runner' but the code reads the TOML itself via fs::read_to_string(&resolved) and a parallel resolve_default_path_under helper (not Keybinds::default_path()). Mental revert: if runner.rs:417 reverted to Keybinds::load(runner), all 3 F-01 tests still pass because they never go through runner.rs:417 or load_layered. The M225/M226 lesson recurs: the fix is at the source level but the test does not pin the production wiring. Contrast with F-02 (m222_f02_settings_keybinds_view.rs): the 5 tests render through the production renderer (terminal.draw -> compute_view -> render -> render_settings_lane -> render_keybinds_view); a revert of the render_settings_lane wiring would cause all 5 to fail. F-02 is production-path tested; F-01 is library-only. Fix: add a test that constructs an in-process MpRunner (or mocks runner.run to return a synthetic JSON), calls Keybinds::load_layered(&runner) directly, and asserts the resulting app.keybinds reflects both the TOML override and the JSON legacy layer. Also assert Keybinds::default_path() is the path load_layered actually reads (so a future regression in default_path resolution is caught).
